findings.text: Provides a single interrupt invalidate operation that refreshes configuration for a supplied interrupt object within supplied guest context and reports the refresh outcome.

Provides a distributor wide invalidate that visits every resident large physical interrupt, refreshes each one, releases references, and additionally invalidates virtual processing element state when present on the calling processor. Observed logic always reports success.
Provides a generic register field sanitiser that isolates a masked shifted field, transforms it through a caller supplied function, and merges the result back while preserving surrounding bits.
Provides a partial wide register update that replaces the byte range selected by offset and length with low bits of a supplied value while preserving untouched bits.

Central command dispatcher decodes command type and routes to device, collection, translation, move, discard, clear, bulk move, trigger, single and bulk invalidate handlers, treats synchronisation as immediate success, and leaves unknown types as device missing failure.

Memory mapped register table exposes control, identifier, type, command base, writer, reader, table base and identification extension views with defined access widths, routing each view to dedicated read and write helpers, ignoring writes to read only views and permitting privileged reader pointer restore.

An event identifier is accepted only when numerically below a per device power of two bound and when its computed guest table address lies in a visible mapped region; otherwise the mapping request is rejected.

Translation mapping selects interrupt number from physical identifier for the translated variant and from event identifier otherwise, enforces distributor minimum and property table maximum bounds, succeeds silently when the translation already exists, creates a missing collection after bounds validation, binds to the target processor when the collection is already mapped, and rolls back fresh collection and translation on allocation or registration failure.

Device mapping validates the device identifier against the device table, limits requested event bit count, discards prior device state on remap to model cache invalidation, treats clear valid as unmap completing with table entry clear, and otherwise installs a new device record with address and size.

Collection mapping with clear valid removes the collection and invalidates cached translations, while set valid resolves the target processor by identifier, fails when that processor is absent, creates the collection after table bounds validation or updates the existing target and refreshes affinity.

Clear and single invalidate require an existing device plus event translation and fail otherwise; clear deasserts software pending state and forwards to the host controller when backed by hardware, while invalidate delegates to configuration refresh.

Bulk invalidate requires a mapped collection and refreshes every interrupt through the owning processor context; bulk move requires two valid distinct processors, does nothing when identical, otherwise migrates every interrupt affinity from the first to the second and invalidates cached translations.

Guest commands are consumed only while enabled, reading fixed size slots sequentially from command base plus reader offset, skipping unreadable slots, advancing the reader by slot size with wrap at the buffer limit until reader meets writer.

Command base and table base writes are ignored while enabled; otherwise they merge partial writes, sanitise shareability and cacheability, enforce fixed page size or alignment, pin entry size and table type, mask read only and unsupported bits, reset queue pointers on command base change, and tear down cached devices or collections plus translation cache when a table base value changes.

Control view reports quiescent when reader equals writer and reports enable state; enable is refused unless device, collection and command bases are all marked valid, disable clears the translation cache and then drains pending commands; writer updates are masked and bounds checked with out of range ignored followed by command drain, while privileged reader restore is rejected when enabled or out of bounds.
Global ITS mutex serialises whole command dispatch and also guards table base change teardown of device and collection lists plus cache invalidation against concurrent save or restore activity.
Command queue mutex serialises command base, writer, reader and control register accesses together with the command drain loop, making pointer and enable updates atomic with processing.

Device, collection and translation records form linked sets: devices carry identifier, table address, event bit count, translation list head and membership link; collections carry identifier, target and membership link; translations carry event identifier, back pointer to collection, interrupt pointer and membership link in the owning device list.

The ITS instance holds device and collection lists, two mutexes for command semantics and queue pointers, device and collection table base values, command base, reader and writer offsets, and an enable flag; queue bounds derive from command base low bits and reader and writer offsets are masked to command alignment.

Mapping lifecycle moves devices from absent to mapped on valid map and back on invalid map or remap with full translation discard, collections from absent to unmapped to mapped on target assignment and back on unmap with dependent translations detached, and translations from absent to installed on map with silent success on duplicate.

Queue lifecycle starts empty with reader and writer zeroed on command base programming, accumulates guest writes to the writer, drains toward quiescent by advancing the reader with wrap, and halts draining while disabled.

Enable lifecycle stays disabled until a control write requests enable with all three bases valid, then enables and drains pending work; any disable request clears enable, invalidates the cache, and attempts a drain that immediately stops.

Resource and guest input hazards include allocation failure during device, collection or translation creation with rollback of partially created objects, duplicate translation treated as benign success, remap or unmap discarding live translations despite specification unpredictability, unreadable guest command slots skipped rather than stalled, and out of range writer or reader values ignored or rejected.

Command queue ABI uses a fixed slot extent of thirty two bytes, a buffer extent computed as low base byte plus one scaled to four kilobyte units, and a pointer mask selecting the offset field within the queue region.

Table and command base ABI pins table type and entry extent fields, forbids indirect collection tables, masks defined read only bit ranges, forces a single sixty four kilobyte page size, aligns the command base, and selects table index zero for devices and one for collections with higher indices reading as zero.

Register access ABI defines control and identifier views as thirty two bit, type, command base, writer, reader and table views as either thirty two or sixty four bit, with the table region spanning sixty four bytes and the identification extension region spanning forty eight bytes.
